title: MD Desk data contract, version 2 (Machinedrum OS 1.63)
description: Plain-data documents exchanged between MD Desk's UI and its data layer. Produced and checked by elektronData (patternToJson/patternFromJson etc.) and mdDataLink::Session::stateToJson. Values are firmware units; see data-contract.md for display units and the mockup mapping. Cross-field limits (length <= totalLength, lock budget, song structure) are checked by elektronData::validate and listed in data-contract.md. Readers must ignore unknown members.

steps64.description: Sorted 0-based step numbers. Below 64 (extended dumps) or 32 (classic dumps).

nameTail.description: Bytes after the name's NUL, only present when not all zero (factory data keeps leftovers).

editAll.description: 1 = one pattern-wide set (ALL), 0 = per-track sets in tracks[].

name.description: Derived from slot; ignored on input.

kit.description: Linked kit, recalled in EXTENDED mode.

locks.description: The pooled parameter locks: at most 64 distinct (track, param), in firmware order.

steps.description: [step, value] for each locked step below totalLength.

firmware.description: P6, contract version 2: what the firmware carries that the editor passes through untouched (dump format bytes, residue, opaque state, undecoded bytes). Readers also take version 1, where these members sit at the top level.

lockedRowsField.description: Opaque firmware byte, 0 in every observed dump.

lockPoolHidden.description: Run-length [count, byte] residue of the lock pool outside the semantic view (unused rows, steps past totalLength). Present only when not canonical; dropped when the lock layout changes.

model.description: OS 1.63 machine id; UW machines have bit 7 set.

machine.description: Manual name (TRX-BD, P-I-SD, ROM-05); derived, ignored on input.

effects.description: AMD AMF EQF EQG FLTF FLTW FLTQ SRR

routing.description: DIST VOL PAN DEL REV LFOS LFOD LFOM

gateBox.description: DVOL PRED DEC DAMP HP LP GATE LEV

rhythmEcho.description: TIME MOD MFRQ FB FILTF FILTW MONO LEV

eq.description: LF LG HF HG PF PG PQ GAIN

dynamix.description: ATCK REL TRHD RTIO KNEE HP OUTG MIX

firmware.description: P6, contract version 2: what the firmware carries that the editor passes through untouched (dump format bytes, residue, opaque state, undecoded bytes). Readers also take version 1, where these members sit at the top level.

items.description: Opaque firmware LFO state, kept as-is.

lfoState.description: Per track: the LFO block's opaque running state (was tracks[].lfo.state in version 1).

repeats.description: pattern: extra passes (REP = repeats + 1); loop: extra passes of the body, 0 = infinite

end.description: Step after the last one played.

tempo.description: BPM, null = keep the previous tempo

target.description: loop: an earlier row; jump: a later row

raw.description: The row's fields as stored (pattern, reserved, repeats, target, mutes, tempo x 24, start, end), only when the kind's fields would not rebuild it.

rows.description: At most 256 rows including the final END.

firmware.description: P6, contract version 2: what the firmware carries that the editor passes through untouched (dump format bytes, residue, opaque state, undecoded bytes). Readers also take version 1, where these members sit at the top level.

routing.description: Per-track output; A-F skip the master effects.

keymap.description: MIDI note -> the MAP EDITOR's target (measured on the firmware, mdDeskFirmwareTest keymap): 0-15 a track's trig, 16-143 a pattern (A01-H16), 144 START, 145 STOP; null is "--" (byte 255). The firmware keeps every other byte as sent (146-254: no effect measured).

control.description: P5: the measured meaning of settings (elektronData::mdGlobalBits), derived and read-only: settings is the value. Change it with {op: globalSet, field, on|v}.

localControl.description: Stored; no effect was seen in the emulator (not verified).

firmware.description: P6, contract version 2: what the firmware carries that the editor passes through untouched (dump format bytes, residue, opaque state, undecoded bytes). Readers also take version 1, where these members sit at the top level.

modulators.description: App-only LFO and random sources and their links to kit parameters (page -> desk).

setup.description: The editor's setup kept with the project (P4, mdDesk/mdDeskSetup.h): the app modulators and the CCs of the eight controller knob rows. Stored by the plug-in as the MDSK chunk of its state.

lifecycle.description: P6: the machine's life as one value (deskCore::Lifecycle): the engine label and the input gate follow it.

capabilities.description: P6: what the engine can do, as data (deskCore::Capabilities), with what the editor does not do yet on any engine (the model's unsupported list) merged in. A page enables a control when can[name] is true and shows reasons[name] otherwise; a name it does not know is not allowed.

sampleAudio.description: P9: the UW sample slots can be read and heard (the emulated machine's memory: their waveforms, sampleWave, and audition on the plug-in's own output; a real Machinedrum ignores SDS dump requests).

sampleLoad.description: P9: a sample file can be sent to a UW ROM slot (SDS).

panic.description: Wave 2: the panic key (every voice off) works on this engine.

playFrom.description: Wave 2: a song can be played from a row (MIDI Stop, a Song Position Pointer and Continue into the machine).

reasons.description: Why a capability is false: the text a disabled control shows.

engines.description: P6: the engine map (the plug-in's engine records), in menu order; empty for a desk outside the plug-in.

history.description: P6: the core's undo history (a gesture is one step).

queued.description: Selected while playing; becomes current at the end of the current pattern.

working.description: edited = not saved on the machine: lost on LOAD KIT or a switch to a pattern linked to another kit.

reloadNeeded.description: The current song's slot was rewritten; heard after STOP, LOAD SONG, PLAY.

patternKits.description: [pattern slot, kit] for every pattern seen in a dump.

desk.description: Added by the desk for the page: the adapter's state (P6: every member declared).

tx.description: An edit is on the wire (waiting for its read-back).

roundTripMs.description: Last edit -> read-back time; -1 before the first.

queued.description: Selected while playing and not heard yet (clears at the playhead wrap).

gridEdit.description: Grid edit (RECORD alone): the RECORD LED is steady.

knobPage.description: DATA ENTRY page: 0 synthesis, 1 effects, 2 routing, -1 unknown.

telemetry.description: Playhead and state come from MD OS 1.63 RAM.

mutes.description: The machine's pattern mutes (P4: read from RAM 0x28b34a when mutesSource is memory).

mutesSource.description: memory: read from the machine (its MUTE window and CCs show too). tracked: what the desk sent and saw.

oneOf.description: The firmware's pattern chain (P4, BANK held + TRIG keys). One bank, each pattern once, loops.

active.description: False after a LOAD PATTERN or a single TRIG with BANK held.

next.description: The entry the firmware queues next.

chain.description: null: not readable on this firmware.

recLock.description: P4, live recording: the trig the last knob turn locks (mdDesk::nextLockStep), for about 3 s.

liveErase.description: Wave 7 and MD-140, live recording: what Delete holds on the machine. param null: EXIT/NO and the track's TRIG key; a kit parameter: EXIT/NO and its DATA ENTRY knob, preparing while the track is selected and the knob page shown, gaveUp when that page never showed (nothing removed).

bankGroup.description: The machine's BANK GROUP: 0 A-D, 1 E-H, -1 unknown.

input.description: The machine takes the page's commands now (the lifecycle's gate).

midi.description: The firmware answers MIDI: loads run.

lifecycleText.description: What the lifecycle state means for the user, worded by the model.

clipboard.description: P6: what the core's clipboard holds (the page's Paste reads it); kit/pattern: the slot it was copied from.

stepsSize.description: The copied block of steps: its tracks and its steps (a selection is steps x tracks; a track page is one track); null when no steps are copied.

song.description: The song slot a song copy was taken from (0.6); null when none.

track.description: COPY what (0.6, trackCopy): the track the parts were copied from, the parts (mdDesk::trackParts names) and what they hold (trigs, accent, swing and slide steps, locked steps); null when none.

global.description: The global slot the GLOBAL page's Copy took (0.6); null when none.

contract.description: The page protocol's version (the contract document's): bumped when a member is renamed, removed or re-meant; adding one keeps it. A page reads it first.

audioDevices.description: The standalone's audio and MIDI devices (P6, mdJucePlugin/mdAudioMidiLink.cpp; data-contract.md 4.8). Not machine data. In a plug-in only schema, version and standalone:false.

clips.description: MD-033: the clips the machine's LCD draws between two value boxes whose parameters depend on each other: i joins parameters i and i + 1 (0-23: SYNTHESIS, EFFECTS, ROUTING). Measured on OS 1.63 (gapProbesFirmwareTest w12clip).

enums.description: P6: the named values the page shows (elektronData/mdNames.h).

slots.description: P6: how many documents of each kind (the model's kind records).

message.description: P6: every message the plug-in sends the Machinedrum Editor page (Bridge gm.recv). Checked by mdDeskTest against what the desk publishes.

oneOf.description: The machine table, once after ready.

pending.description: The document shows an edit submitted to the machine and not yet read back (P6: pending, published merged over observed).

slot.description: The slot; for the working kit, the kit it was loaded from.

source.description: P6: where the observed document came from.

oneOf.description: A document: a stored slot (pattern, kit, song, global) or the kit that plays (workingKit, P6).

P6: a question before something is lost. The page shows message with a confirm button; confirm resends command with force, which answers every question the command raised: a command that loses two things asks once, naming both (also). alternatives: other ways to go on, each its own button: the page sends its first commands, then command with force (loadKit: Save and load = saveKit first).

also.description: Other questions this one answers too (force answers all of them).

alternatives.description: Other ways to go on, each a button: label, and the commands sent before command with force.

songRow.description: 0.3.5: the song row heard (RAM 0x2b18f5, md::SongPosition, as it was at PLAY and at the last wrap: the byte queues the next row two steps early), null where the engine cannot read it. Meaningful while machine.songMode is true and the machine plays.

songRepeats.description: 0.6 (MD-147): the passes of that row still to come (RAM 0x2b1901, md::SongPosition, counting down: REPEATS 3 reads 3, 2, 1, 0), read with songRow; null when songRow is.

oneOf.description: B-030: the host's tempo (a DAW's playhead, also while its transport is stopped), when it changed or the page is new. follows: the plug-in sets the machine to follow the host's clock (a DAW, not the standalone).

I-018: the CPU meter in the top bar, a few times a second while the page is up: the share of each audio block's real-time budget the host's processBlock call spends (load: smoothed over about half a second; worst: the largest single block in the last 3 s; 1 = the whole budget; null unless running), whether the host runs the audio (state: none before the first block, stopped when blocks stopped coming, bypassed, offline while it renders), and the popover's details: the machine's speed (realtime), the host's rate and block size, the speed-ups as the machine runs them (on, off, some: leversOff names the ones off; unknown with no machine), L3 (exactEssi) and whether the editor runs translated (Rosetta).

saved.description: The speed-up switches as saved in the plug-in's settings (what the next session starts with): legacyEmulation (the speed-ups off), leversOff (by their environment variable's suffix).

oneOf.description: 0.6 (GLOBAL › Map editor › LEARN, I-002): a note on that reached the plug-in from outside (the host's MIDI in or a MIDI input port), as it came: ch 0-15, note, vel 1-127. Sent on the next step (every 20 ms or so) while the page is up; a burst past 16 a step, or past the plug-in's queue, is dropped. The page's own keyboard is not in it.

I-002, B-062: the notes held down from outside (the host's MIDI in or a MIDI input port), each with its channel (0-15), by channel then low to high: a note on holds a note until its note off (or all notes off, all sound off, a system reset). A state, not events: sent when it changed, looked at every 32 ms (a burst is one message), and once for a new page; a note off is never lost, and a MIDI input that changes or closes, a bypass or a release lets go of every note. Not in HW MIDI (what comes in is the real machine's own MIDI OUT). The page's own keyboard is not in it. The Monomachine Editor lights, on the Perform keyboard, the notes on the channels the machine plays (AUTO, the track channels, MULTI TRIG, MULTI MAP).

I-021: the LCD's output meter and volume, every 250 ms while the page is up: peakL and peakR, the largest sample of the main output's left and right since the previous message, after the volume (linear, 1 = 0 dBFS; 0 when the audio does not run or the channel is not enabled); clip, whether a sample of any output (main and extra) was above 0 dBFS in that time; gainDb, the volume (the plug-in's output gain after the emulation, -60 to +6 dB in 0.1 dB steps; null when it is off). Set with the outputGain command.

B-035: how the host runs the plug-in's audio, once a second while the machine starts and for the first minute: the host's audio calls (blocks, bypassed ones apart) and the machine's speed (realtime: machine seconds per wall second, null before the first block). The start-up card says when a plug-in gets no audio, or the machine is slower than real time.
The firmware's own LCD while it starts: 128 x 64, one bit a pixel, row-major, base64.
P7: the plug-in's verdict on a firmware file the user chose or dropped (checked, copied into the ROM folder; it never leaves the computer).
LOAD ROM: which firmware image the machine runs and where it is (the answer to romInfo). REMOVE only deletes inside the editor's ROM folder (inFolder).

I-008: the editor's menu (the answer to openMenu), as data: the page draws it where it was asked for (skins/shared/deskMenu.js) and sends the chosen entry back as menuPick {menu, n}; the window runs it. The same tree is the menu bar's and, when no page is up, a native menu (mdEditorMenu.h).

menu.description: this menu's number: a pick of an older menu does nothing

title.description: the first line: which editor and its version (not an entry)

id.description: stable (zoom-in, open-log-folder): the page's journeys find an entry by it

key.description: the shortcut's words, shown at the right (a submenu: what it is set to)

n.description: an entry that can run: the number menuPick sends back

items.description: a submenu's entries, of this same shape

oneOf.description: Something the plug-in has for the user (a question or a warning), shown as the page's modal instead of a native alert; the button pressed goes back as noticeAnswer {notice: this id, button} (the request's own id is its result's). The first button is the answer to a question, the last the safe one.

id.description: the notice's number, from 1; a banner with no title and no text (it takes the banner away) has 0: it waits for no answer

modal.description: false: a banner (no backdrop, the page usable under it; DESIGN-updates.md), not the dialog; absent: the dialog. A banner with no title and no text takes the banner away.

oneOf.description: Where the web view has no page zoom of its own (Linux's webkit2gtk): the page's CSS zoom, the zoom that fits the page's design size into the window times the user's zoom (mdPageZoom.h), sent when it changes and again when the page starts again; the page sets document.documentElement.style.zoom (skins/shared/deskZoom.js). Never sent where the web view zooms itself (macOS, WebView2).

zoom.description: greater than 0; 1: the page's own size

oneOf.description: Files dropped on the window (macOS for now; FOUNDATION.md, Files dropped on the window). The window keeps them and says what each is; the page decides what each becomes and answers with dropRom, dropSyx or dropSample, which name a file by this message's drop and the file's n, never by a path (each file serves once, as the kind it was dropped as, until the next drop or 10 minutes without use). x and y: where they were dropped, in the page's CSS pixels.

drop.description: this drop's number: the drop commands name it

n.description: the file's number in the drop, from 0

kind.description: by the extension, in any case: rom .bin .zip, sysex .syx, sample .wav .wave .aif .aiff .aifc

name.description: the file's name, never its folder

oneOf.description: Files the window takes are dragged over it (active true), or have left it (false; a drop message ends it too): the page shows where a drop goes.

P7, B-019: a .syx file the user chose or dropped, parsed by the plug-in: what it holds (per kind the items with their slot, name, format bytes, whether they overwrite data or play now) and what cannot be sent and why. It informs; the import sends the chosen messages to the machine as they are.

place.description: 0.6: SPECIFIC place, per kind the first slot its items land in (empty: each in its own slot); then each item's slot is where it lands and its from the file's slot

reset.description: 0.6: Reset machine… (Empty reset, Factory reset): the preview of what the reset sends, which already runs

oneOf.description: P7, B-019: an import's progress: before (the slots the editor has not read are read first), send (messages handed to the machine of the chosen ones), read (documents read back), done (with the report: per outcome a count, and a line for each item the machine did not take as in the file).

kind.description: 0.3.5: while running, the kind of the item at work (the one the next message belongs to, or the one read now)

kinds.description: 0.3.5: while running, per kind of the import the phase's items done of its total (send: items whose every message went; before, read: items read)

check.description: 0.6: VERIFY ONLY (nothing sent; the report counts same, differs, unknown, no reply)

oneOf.description: P7: an export to a .syx: written, or why not. 0.6: running while the Monomachine's DigiPRO waveforms are read from the machine (the text says how far), then the last one says what was written.

0.6 (wave 6): the export panel's facts (syxExportInfo): per kind (global, kit, pattern, song; wave on the Monomachine) its slots, how many the editor holds, how many hold data and the first and last of those (-1: none).

0.6 (wave 6): a factory reset being prepared (the Machinedrum: a second machine started from the user's ROM is read; prepare, with the dumps read of all) or failing (failed, with why). The reset itself follows as a syxPreview with reset and syxProgress.
The plug-in's MIDI learn mappings (host).

enabled.description: MIDI mapping (MIDI learn and the Control workspace) is on; the pages hide both unless true (mdmm::midiMappingEnabled, deskHost.h).

oneOf.description: The engine changed: the page starts its documents over.
The standalone's audio and MIDI devices (host, mdAudioMidiLink).
The window asks the page to open its AUDIO / MIDI panel.
P9: the UW sample slots (md-desk/samples).

P9: one slot's waveform at the width the page draws it (after sampleWave): min, max per bin of its own samples, 16-bit. The overview in md-desk/samples has 128 bins a slot; this is the detail, for one slot, on demand.

bins.description: Pairs in peaks: the bins asked for, at most the slot's length (a bin is at least one sample); 0 for an empty slot.

oneOf.description: P9: the audition (after audition): playing when it starts (from the start, at the slot's own rate, on the plug-in's own output), stopped when it is stopped, plays out, is replaced by another or the device is gone. Two messages an audition, never per frame: the page moves its playhead from rate itself.

P9: a sample file on its way to a ROM slot (SDS), after chooseSample: sending (sent of total packets), then done, failed or cancelled. A refusal before it starts is failed with only slot, file and text.

slot.description: The ROM slot, 0-47 (48-51: a RAM slot asked for, refused).

handshake.description: false: the machine did not answer the header, the packets go without a handshake (open loop).

notes.description: What the conversion changed (mono, rate, cut), in plain words.

command.description: Generated from the model's command table and the plug-in's (deskHost), P6: every command the page may send.

host: look for the ROM again
host
host: choose the firmware file (.bin, or a .zip with it): the window's native file chooser; the file stays on this computer
host: which firmware is installed (answered with a romInfo message): the LOAD ROM dialog
host: delete the firmware from the editor's ROM folder (never outside it); the machine stops and the start-up card asks for a ROM again

host: the button pressed on the notice numbered notice (a notice message's id: the plug-in's own question or warning, shown by the page); refused when that notice waits for no answer (answered already, or replaced) or has no such button
host: choose a .syx to import: the window's native file chooser; a preview follows (syxPreview)

host: choose a sample (WAV or AIFF) for UW ROM slot slot: the window's native file chooser; the plug-in reads the file, converts it and sends it as SDS (sampleLoad messages follow); the file never passes through the page

host: import the previewed .syx: the kinds chosen (global, kit, pattern, song, other) but the items in skip ("kind:slot", the slot an item lands in), sent to the machine as they are (the firmware decides what it takes), then read back and reported (syxProgress); no undo step. placeAt (SPECIFIC, 0.6): per kind the first slot its items land in, in slot order ({"kit": 4}; the dumps go with that position byte and checksum); checkOnly (VERIFY ONLY): nothing is sent, each item's slot is read and compared with the file
host: stop an import: nothing more is sent, what went is read back and reported

host: the open .syx's preview again (syxPreview) with its items placed: per kind the first slot ({"kit": 4, "pattern": 16}), a kind not named in its own slots; each item says where it lands (slot), where it came from (from), whether it overwrites data there; an item past the last slot does not land

host: the documents the editor holds as one .syx, through the window's native save dialog: every one (no kinds), or the kinds named (global, kit, pattern, song; the Monomachine's DigiPRO waveforms as wave, read from the machine) with their ranges ({"kit": [0, 11]}, from 0, inclusive; a kind without one: all its slots); syxExport messages follow
host: the export panel's facts (a syxExportInfo message): per kind its slots, how many the editor holds, how many hold data and the first and last of those

samples.description: P9 (data-contract.md 4.9): the UW sample slots as read from the emulated machine's memory: ROM slots from flash, RAM buffers from DSP2's memory. Published when it changes and after every ready; a real Machinedrum has none (capabilities.sampleAudio).

capacity.description: Samples DSP2's sample memory holds in all (ROM slots and the four RAM buffers share it).

ramReason.description: Why the RAM buffers are not shown (empty when they are).
